## Data Cleaning, Missing Values, and Type Conversions

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
import warnings
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display

# Suppress warnings (like DtypeWarning)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Load dataset
csv_path  = Path("Data/lightcast_job_postings.csv")
df = pd.read_csv(csv_path, low_memory=False)

# Helper function for missing value summary
def missing_summary(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ms = frame.isna().mean().mul(100).round(1).rename("% missing")
    dt = frame.dtypes.astype(str).rename("dtype")
    return pd.concat([dt, ms], axis=1).sort_values("% missing", ascending=False)

# Baseline snapshot (before cleaning)
rows_before, cols_before = df.shape
missing_cells_before = int(df.isna().sum().sum())
baseline_overview = pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": ["rows","columns","total missing cells"],
    "before": [rows_before, cols_before, missing_cells_before]
})
baseline_top_missing = missing_summary(df).head(12)

# Show initial outputs
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 1: Preview of raw dataset (first 5 rows)": []}))
display(df.head())
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 2: Baseline dataset overview": []}))
display(baseline_overview)
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 3: Top 12 most-missing columns (before cleaning)": []}))
display(baseline_top_missing)

# ============================
# Cleaning & Conversions
# ============================

# Standardize column names
df.columns = (df.columns.str.strip()
              .str.replace(r"\s+", "_", regex=True)
              .str.upper())

# Drop irrelevant columns
to_drop = ["ID","URL","ACTIVE_URLS","DUPLICATES","LAST_UPDATED_TIMESTAMP",
           "NAICS2","NAICS3","NAICS4","NAICS5","NAICS6","SOC_2","SOC_3","SOC_5"]
df.drop(columns=[c for c in to_drop if c in df.columns],
        inplace=True, errors="ignore")

# Convert dates
for col in [c for c in ["POSTED","UPDATED","DATE","JOB_POST_DATE"] if c in df.columns]:
    df[col] = pd.to_datetime(df[col], errors="coerce")

# Convert salary columns
for col in ["SALARY","MINSALARY","MAXSALARY","ANNUAL_SALARY","HOURLY_RATE","PAY"]:
    if col in df.columns:
        df[col] = (df[col].astype(str)
                   .str.replace(r"[^0-9.\-]", "", regex=True)
                   .replace({"": np.nan, "-": np.nan})
                   .astype(float))

# Drop columns with >50% missing
df.dropna(axis=1, thresh=int(len(df)*0.5), inplace=True)

# Fill missing numeric values
num_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
if num_cols:
    if "INDUSTRY" in df.columns:
        df[num_cols] = df[num_cols].fillna(df.groupby("INDUSTRY")[num_cols].transform("median"))
    df[num_cols] = df[num_cols].fillna(df[num_cols].median())

# Fill missing categoricals with "Unknown"
for c in df.select_dtypes(include=["object"]).columns:
    df[c] = df[c].fillna("Unknown")

# Remove duplicates by key fields
dup_key = [c for c in ["TITLE","COMPANY","LOCATION","POSTED"] if c in df.columns]
if dup_key:
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=dup_key, keep="first")

# Snapshot after cleaning
rows_after, cols_after = df.shape
missing_cells_after = int(df.isna().sum().sum())
summary_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": ["rows","columns","total missing cells"],
    "before": [rows_before, cols_before, missing_cells_before],
    "after":  [rows_after,  cols_after,  missing_cells_after]
})
after_top_missing = missing_summary(df).head(12)

# Show cleaned outputs
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 4: Cleaned dataset preview (first 5 rows)": []}))
display(df.head())
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 5: Dataset summary (before vs after cleaning)": []}))
display(summary_table)
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 6: Top 12 most-missing columns (after cleaning)": []}))
display(after_top_missing)
```


## Identifying and removing redundant columns, duplicates, and extreme values

```{python}
#| echo: false
import re, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display

# Ensure dataset is loaded
try:
    df
except NameError:
    df = pd.read_csv("Data/lightcast_job_postings.csv", low_memory=False)

# ============================
# Step 7: Remove Redundant Columns
# ============================

rows_before, cols_before = df.shape

explicit_drops = [
    "ID","URL","ACTIVE_URLS","DUPLICATES","LAST_UPDATED_TIMESTAMP",
    "TITLE_RAW","COMPANY_RAW","MODELED_EXPIRED","MODELED_DURATION",
    "NAICS2","NAICS2_NAME","NAICS3","NAICS3_NAME","NAICS4","NAICS4_NAME","NAICS5","NAICS5_NAME",
    "COUNTY_OUTGOING","COUNTY_NAME_OUTGOING","COUNTY_INCOMING","COUNTY_NAME_INCOMING",
    "MSA_OUTGOING","MSA_NAME_OUTGOING","MSA_INCOMING","MSA_NAME_INCOMING",
    "SOURCE_TYPES","SOURCES","TITLE_CLEAN"
]

flow_drop = [c for c in df.columns if re.search(r"(OUTGOING|INCOMING)$", c, flags=re.I)]

canon_keep = set()
for col in ["TITLE","COMPANY","LOCATION","POSTED","REMOTE_TYPE_NAME","EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME",
            "NAICS6_NAME","CITY_NAME","COUNTY_NAME","MSA_NAME","STATE","STATE_NAME"]:
    if col in df.columns:
        canon_keep.add(col)

name_dupes = []
for base, alt in [("TITLE","TITLE_NAME"), ("COMPANY","COMPANY_NAME")]:
    if base in df.columns and alt in df.columns and alt not in canon_keep:
        name_dupes.append(alt)

to_drop = sorted(set([c for c in explicit_drops if c in df.columns] + flow_drop + name_dupes))
df.drop(columns=to_drop, inplace=True, errors="ignore")

rows_after_cols, cols_after_cols = df.shape
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 7: Redundant columns removed (preview)": []}))
display(pd.DataFrame({"Dropped Columns": to_drop[:40]}))
display(pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": ["rows","columns"],
    "before": [rows_before, cols_before],
    "after":  [rows_after_cols, cols_after_cols]
}))

# ============================
# Step 8: Remove Duplicates
# ============================

rows_before_dedup = len(df)
dedupe_key = [c for c in ["TITLE","COMPANY","LOCATION","POSTED"] if c in df.columns]
if not dedupe_key:
    dedupe_key = [c for c in ["TITLE","COMPANY","CITY_NAME","STATE","POSTED"] if c in df.columns]

df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=dedupe_key, keep="first")
rows_after_dedup = len(df)

display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 8: Deduplication summary": []}))
display(pd.DataFrame({
    "dedupe_key_used": [", ".join(dedupe_key) if dedupe_key else "(none)"],
    "rows_removed": [rows_before_dedup - rows_after_dedup],
    "rows_after": [rows_after_dedup]
}))


#| echo: false
import re, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display

# ============================
# Step 9: Remove Extreme Values (Outliers) — Robust detection
# ============================

# Ensure salary-related columns are still in the dataset
df.columns = [c.strip().upper() for c in df.columns]

# Reload original salary info if needed
if not any(c in df.columns for c in ["SALARY","SALARY_FROM","SALARY_TO","ORIGINAL_PAY_PERIOD"]):
    try:
        df_raw = pd.read_csv("Data/lightcast_job_postings.csv", low_memory=False)
        df_raw.columns = [c.strip().upper() for c in df_raw.columns]
        for c in ["SALARY","SALARY_FROM","SALARY_TO","ORIGINAL_PAY_PERIOD"]:
            if c in df_raw.columns and c not in df.columns:
                df[c] = df_raw[c]
    except Exception as e:
        display(pd.DataFrame({"⚠️ Warning": [f"Could not reload salary columns: {e}"]}))

# Detect any salary-related columns again
salary_cols = [c for c in df.columns if re.search(r"SALARY|PAY|WAGE", c, flags=re.I)]

if not salary_cols:
    display(pd.DataFrame({"⚠️ Warning": ["No salary-related columns found. Skipping Step 9."]}))
else:
    # 1️⃣ Coerce salary values to numeric
    for col in ["SALARY", "SALARY_FROM", "SALARY_TO"]:
        if col in df.columns:
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

    # 2️⃣ Compute midpoint
    if {"SALARY_FROM","SALARY_TO"}.issubset(df.columns):
        df["SALARY_MID"] = df[["SALARY_FROM","SALARY_TO"]].mean(axis=1)
    elif "SALARY" in df.columns:
        df["SALARY_MID"] = df["SALARY"]
    else:
        df["SALARY_MID"] = np.nan

    # 3️⃣ Convert to annual
    def to_annual(v, period):
        if pd.isna(v): 
            return np.nan
        p = str(period).lower() if pd.notna(period) else "year"
        factor = {"hour":2080, "day":260, "week":52, "month":12, "year":1}.get(p, 1)
        return float(v) * factor

    if "ORIGINAL_PAY_PERIOD" in df.columns:
        df["ANNUAL_SALARY"] = [to_annual(v, p) for v, p in zip(df["SALARY_MID"], df["ORIGINAL_PAY_PERIOD"])]
    else:
        df["ANNUAL_SALARY"] = df["SALARY_MID"]

    df.loc[df["ANNUAL_SALARY"] <= 0, "ANNUAL_SALARY"] = np.nan

    # 4️⃣ IQR outlier handling
    s = df["ANNUAL_SALARY"].dropna()
    low = high = np.nan
    removed_outliers = 0
    if len(s) > 0:
        q1, q3 = s.quantile([0.25, 0.75])
        iqr = q3 - q1
        low, high = q1 - 1.5 * iqr, q3 + 1.5 * iqr
        mask = (df["ANNUAL_SALARY"] < low) | (df["ANNUAL_SALARY"] > high)
        removed_outliers = int(mask.sum())
        df.loc[mask, "ANNUAL_SALARY"] = np.nan

    # 5️⃣ Display summary
    display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 9: Salary Outlier Summary (IQR)": []}))
    display(pd.DataFrame({
        "salary_column_used": ["ANNUAL_SALARY"],
        "iqr_low_threshold": [low],
        "iqr_high_threshold": [high],
        "values_set_to_NaN": [removed_outliers],
        "remaining_with_salary": [int(df["ANNUAL_SALARY"].notna().sum())]
    }))


# ============================
# Step 10: Save Cleaned Dataset
# ============================

out_path = "Data/lightcast_clean_final.csv"
df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)
display(pd.DataFrame({"📌 Step 10: Cleaned dataset saved": [out_path]}))

```

# Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with visualizations

```{python}
#| echo: false
import re, numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

# Use cleaned df if present; otherwise load the saved clean file
try:
    df
except NameError:
    df = pd.read_csv("Data/lightcast_clean_final.csv", low_memory=False)

# Normalize column names
df.columns = [c.strip().upper() for c in df.columns]

def H(txt):  # proper headings (no tables/dashes)
    display(Markdown(f"### {txt}"))

def note(msg):
    display(Markdown(f"*ℹ️ {msg}*"))

# 3.1 Missing Values Heatmap ---------------------------------------
#| echo: false
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

try:
    df
except NameError:
    df = pd.read_csv("Data/lightcast_clean_final.csv", low_memory=False)

df.columns = [c.strip().upper() for c in df.columns]

display(Markdown("### 3.1 Missing Values Heatmap"))

# Top 30 columns by % missing (keeps heatmap readable)
top_cols = (df.isna().mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(30).index.tolist())
if not top_cols:
    display(Markdown("*ℹ️ No columns with missing values to visualize.*"))
else:
    sample = df[top_cols].isna().astype(int)
    if len(sample) > 1000:
        sample = sample.sample(1000, random_state=0)

    fig = px.imshow(
        sample.T,
        color_continuous_scale=["#2ca02c", "#d62728"],  # Present → Missing
        aspect="auto",
        labels=dict(x="Row (sampled)", y="Columns", color="Missing"),
        title="Missing Values Heatmap (Top 30 Columns, up to 1,000 rows)"
    )
    fig.update_coloraxes(cmin=0, cmax=1, colorbar=dict(tickvals=[0,1], ticktext=["Present","Missing"]))
    fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=40, b=10))
    fig.show()

# 3.2 Job Postings by Industry ---------------------------------------
H("3.2 Job Postings by Industry")

naics_cols = [c for c in ["NAICS_2022_6_NAME","NAICS6_NAME","NAICS_NAME","NAICS4_NAME"] if c in df.columns]
if naics_cols:
    ind_col = naics_cols[0]
    top_ind = (df[ind_col].dropna().astype(str).str.strip()
               .replace("", np.nan).dropna()
               .value_counts().head(15).rename("postings").to_frame().reset_index()
               .rename(columns={"index": ind_col}))
    display(top_ind.set_index(ind_col))

    fig = px.bar(
        top_ind.sort_values("postings"),
        x="postings", y=ind_col, orientation="h",
        title="Top 15 Industries by Job Postings",
        text="postings"
    )
    # NOTE: escape Plotly placeholders in f-strings using double braces
    fig.update_traces(
        texttemplate="%{text:,}",
        hovertemplate=f"{ind_col}: %{{y}}<br>Postings: %{{x:,}}<extra></extra>"
    )
    fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, yaxis_title="", xaxis_title="Number of Postings",
                      margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
    fig.show()
else:
    note("No NAICS name columns found (e.g., **NAICS_2022_6_NAME**). Skipping industry plots.")

# 3.3 Salary Distribution by Industry --------------------------------
H("3.3 Salary Distribution by Industry")

if ("ANNUAL_SALARY" in df.columns) and naics_cols:
    ind_col = naics_cols[0]
    dtemp = df[[ind_col,"ANNUAL_SALARY"]].dropna()
    top8 = dtemp[ind_col].value_counts().head(8).index
    dbox = dtemp[dtemp[ind_col].isin(top8)]
    if len(dbox) > 0:
        fig = px.box(
            dbox, x=ind_col, y="ANNUAL_SALARY",
            title="Annual Salary by Industry (Top 8 by postings)",
            points=False
        )
        fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, xaxis_title="", yaxis_title="Annual Salary",
                          margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
        fig.update_traces(
            hovertemplate=f"{ind_col}: %{{x}}<br>Annual Salary: %{{y:,}}<extra></extra>"
        )
        fig.show()

        stats = (dbox.groupby(ind_col)["ANNUAL_SALARY"]
                    .agg(n="count", median="median",
                         p25=lambda s: s.quantile(0.25), p75=lambda s: s.quantile(0.75))
                    .sort_values("n", ascending=False))
        display(stats)
    else:
        note("Not enough salary data by industry to plot.")
else:
    note("**ANNUAL_SALARY** or a NAICS name column is missing. Skipping salary-by-industry.")

# 3.4 Remote vs. On-Site Jobs ----------------------------------------
H("3.4 Remote vs. On-Site Jobs")

rt_col = next((c for c in ["REMOTE_TYPE_NAME","REMOTE_TYPE"] if c in df.columns), None)
if rt_col:
    counts = (df[rt_col].fillna("Unknown").astype(str).str.strip()
              .value_counts().rename_axis(rt_col).reset_index(name="postings"))
    display(counts.set_index(rt_col))

    fig = px.pie(
        counts, names=rt_col, values="postings",
        title="Remote vs. On-Site Job Postings", hole=0.35
    )
    fig.update_traces(
        textposition="inside",
        textinfo="percent+label",
        hovertemplate="%{label}: %{value:,}<extra></extra>"
    )
    fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
    fig.show()
else:
    note("**REMOTE_TYPE_NAME** not found. Skipping remote vs. on-site chart.")

# 3.5 Job Postings Over Time (interactive) ----------------------------
H("3.5 Job Postings Over Time")

date_col = next((c for c in ["POSTED","DATE","JOB_POST_DATE","LAST_UPDATED_DATE"] if c in df.columns), None)
if date_col:
    ts = df[[date_col]].copy()
    ts[date_col] = pd.to_datetime(ts[date_col], errors="coerce")
    ts = ts.dropna()
    if len(ts) > 0:
        monthly = ts.set_index(date_col).resample("MS").size().rename("postings").reset_index()

        # ✅ FIX: use the column name string directly (not date_col.name)
        display(monthly.tail(12).set_index(date_col))

        fig = px.line(monthly, x=date_col, y="postings", title="Job Postings Trend (Monthly)")
        fig.update_traces(hovertemplate="%{x|%b %Y}: %{y:,}<extra></extra>")
        fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, xaxis_title="Month", yaxis_title="Number of Postings",
                          margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
        fig.show()
    else:
        note("All POSTED dates are invalid or missing after parsing.")
else:
    note("No date column (e.g., **POSTED**) available. Skipping time series.")


# 3.6 Top Companies ---------------------------------------------------
H("3.6 Top Companies")

comp_col = next((c for c in ["COMPANY_NAME","COMPANY"] if c in df.columns), None)
if comp_col:
    top_comp = (df[comp_col].dropna().astype(str).str.strip()
                .replace("", np.nan).dropna()
                .value_counts().head(15).rename("postings").to_frame().reset_index()
                .rename(columns={"index": comp_col}))
    display(top_comp.set_index(comp_col))

    fig = px.bar(
        top_comp.sort_values("postings"),
        x="postings", y=comp_col, orientation="h",
        title="Top 15 Companies by Job Postings", text="postings"
    )
    fig.update_traces(
        texttemplate="%{text:,}",
        hovertemplate=f"{comp_col}: %{{y}}<br>Postings: %{{x:,}}<extra></extra>"
    )
    fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, yaxis_title="", xaxis_title="Number of Postings",
                      margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
    fig.show()
else:
    note("Company column not found. Skipping top companies.")

# 3.7 Job Postings by State ------------------------------------------
H("3.7 Job Postings by State")

state_col = next((c for c in ["STATE_NAME","STATE"] if c in df.columns), None)
if state_col:
    top_states = (df[state_col].dropna().astype(str).str.strip()
                  .replace("", np.nan).dropna()
                  .value_counts().head(15).rename("postings").to_frame().reset_index()
                  .rename(columns={"index": state_col}))
    display(top_states.set_index(state_col))

    fig = px.bar(
        top_states.sort_values("postings"),
        x="postings", y=state_col, orientation="h",
        title="Top 15 States by Job Postings", text="postings"
    )
    fig.update_traces(
        texttemplate="%{text:,}",
        hovertemplate=f"{state_col}: %{{y}}<br>Postings: %{{x:,}}<extra></extra>"
    )
    fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, yaxis_title="", xaxis_title="Number of Postings",
                      margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
    fig.show()
else:
    note("Neither **STATE_NAME** nor **STATE** is available. Skipping geography plot.")

# 3.8 Most Requested Skills ------------------------------------------
H("3.8 Most Requested Skills")

skills_col = next((c for c in ["SKILLS_NAME","SPECIALIZED_SKILLS_NAME","COMMON_SKILLS_NAME","SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME"]
                   if c in df.columns), None)
if skills_col:
    s = df[skills_col].dropna().astype(str)
    s = (s.str.replace(r"\[|\]", "", regex=True)
          .str.replace('"', "", regex=False)
          .str.replace(r"\\n", " ", regex=True)
          .str.split(r"\s*,\s*|\|")
          .explode()
          .str.strip()
          .replace("", np.nan)
          .dropna())

    top_skills = s.value_counts().head(20).rename("MENTIONS").to_frame().reset_index()
    top_skills.columns = ["SKILL","MENTIONS"]
    display(top_skills.set_index("SKILL"))

    fig = px.bar(
        top_skills.sort_values("MENTIONS"),
        x="MENTIONS", y="SKILL", orientation="h",
        title="Top 20 Requested Skills", text="MENTIONS"
    )
    fig.update_traces(
        texttemplate="%{text:,}",
        hovertemplate="Skill: %{y}<br>Mentions: %{x:,}<extra></extra>"
    )
    fig.update_layout(title_x=0.02, yaxis_title="", xaxis_title="Mentions in Postings",
                      margin=dict(l=10,r=10,b=10,t=40))
    fig.show()
else:
    note("No skills columns found (e.g., **SKILLS_NAME**). Skipping skills analysis.")


```
